evidence: The exact versioned profile covers projects, corpus items, documents, evidence records, decisions, tasks, dossiers, and exports. Current state plus command selects at most one destination; callers cannot supply the destination.

Python and TypeScript validators reject malformed, unknown, illegal, stale, or mismatched input before the persistence callback. Successful transitions retain bounded actor, reason, canonical UTC time, idempotency identity, and revision prior+1 in an owned immutable result.

The architecture guide contains explicit Mermaid diagrams for all eight subjects and documents every terminal state, permitted reopen rule, irreversible terminal, stable error behavior, and restart composition.
All 25 TypeScript contract tests, 30 Python contract tests, and 35 service tests passed at the exact candidate.

Material boundaries include illegal command before persistence, optimistic revision conflict, unknown state, aggregate mismatch, path-bearing actor, control-character reason, unknown field, immutable ownership, explicit terminal reopen, irreversible deletion, and restart at the emitted revision.

The language-neutral schema now declares profile, snapshot, command, actor/reason, and emitted-transition wire shapes; the exact profile is bound into generated Python and TypeScript with schema/profile SHA-256 constants.

Documentation, package exports, build-schema inventory, Python quality inventory, sidecar required-module inventory, and its strict packaging test were updated. The transition itself is the portable audit fact carrying actor, reason, time, command, prior/new revision, and idempotency identity.

No persistence schema or migration changed because this task defines the framework-neutral validation boundary and invokes persistence only through a callback after successful validation. No API route, UI, dependency, product scope, or unrelated aggregate behavior was added.
